claims.text: Trajectories of routine biomarkers can flag pre-clinical mobility decline.
claims.poster_quote: Trajectories of routine biomarkers can flag pre-clinical mobility decline.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Functional decline - encompassing gait impairment, reduced mobility, and fall risk - affects more than one-third of adults over 65 and contributes to approximately three million emergency visits and $50 billion in annual U.S. healthcare expenditures.
claims.reason: Section: Introduction. The paper explicitly states that functional decline affects more than one-third of adults over 65, supporting the claim.

claims.text: In All of Us (N = 297,861; 11.1% cases), gradient boosting with trajectory features beat static lab summaries (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755; p < 0.001).
claims.poster_quote: In All of Us (N = 297,861; 11.1% cases), gradient boosting with trajectory features beat static lab summaries (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755; p < 0.001).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: LightGBM models incorporating trajectories significantly outperformed static laboratory summaries (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755; DeLong p < 0.001).
claims.reason: Abstract and Results section. The paper provides the exact AUROC values and p-value, supporting the claim.

claims.text: Each biomarker gave five descriptors - mean, SD, delta, count and slope - yielding 80 trajectory features plus age and gender.
claims.poster_quote: Each biomarker gave five descriptors - mean, SD, delta, count and slope - yielding 80 trajectory features plus age and gender.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Trajectory features captured five per-biomarker descriptors: mean, standard deviation (intra-individual variability), delta (last minus first, directional change), count (measurement frequency), and linear slope (rate of change per day). This yields 80 trajectory features per participant across all concept name variants. Age at index and one-hot encoded gender were included in the combined models.
claims.reason: Methods section: Feature Engineering. The paper explicitly lists the five descriptors and confirms the total number of features and inclusion of age and gender.

claims.text: Four classifiers (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) were trained with 5-fold cross-validation and out-of-fold evaluation.
claims.poster_quote: Four classifiers (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) were trained with 5-fold cross-validation and out-of-fold evaluation.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Four algorithms were evaluated: (1) ℓ2-penalized logistic regression... (2) random forest... (3) XGBoost... and (4) LightGBM... All models were trained with 5-fold stratified cross-validation; out-of-fold (OOF) predictions across all folds were aggregated for unbiased evaluation.
claims.reason: Methods section: Model Development and Evaluation. The paper explicitly describes the four classifiers and the cross-validation approach.

claims.text: Isotonic calibration cut the Brier score to 0.083 from 0.174 without losing discrimination.
claims.poster_quote: Isotonic calibration cut the Brier score to 0.083 from 0.174 without losing discrimination.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Isotonic calibration reduced Brier score from 0.174 to 0.083 (52.3% improvement) without degrading discrimination (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.796).
claims.reason: Results section: Sensitivity analyses and calibration. The paper explicitly states the reduction in Brier score and confirms no loss in discrimination.

claims.text: Using only twelve labs - no diagnosis codes, medications or functional tests - the model works as a passive digital biomarker needing no workflow change.
claims.poster_quote: Using only twelve labs - no diagnosis codes, medications or functional tests - the model works as a passive digital biomarker needing no workflow change.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our model achieves AUROC 0.797 using only twelve laboratory biomarkers - no diagnosis codes, medications, functional assessments, or free-text processing. This constraint is a deliberate design choice: it produces a model that functions as a passive digital biomarker, requiring no new data collection, patient interaction, or clinical workflow modification.
claims.reason: Discussion section. The paper explicitly supports the claim that the model works as a passive digital biomarker without requiring workflow changes.

claims.text: Recent multi-horizon EHR fall-risk models reach AUROC 0.70-0.87 but require diagnosis histories, medication lists and prior fall documentation.
claims.poster_quote: Recent multi-horizon EHR fall-risk models reach AUROC 0.70-0.87 but require diagnosis histories, medication lists and prior fall documentation; our feature-engineered trajectories stay deployable with standard tabular classifiers.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Recent multi-horizon EHR models for fall risk achieve AUROCs of 0.70–0.87, but require diagnosis histories, medication lists, comorbidity scores, and prior fall documentation.
claims.reason: Discussion section. The paper explicitly provides the AUROC range and the required features for recent multi-horizon EHR models.

claims.text: SHAP ranked BMI mean the top physiologic predictor.
claims.poster_quote: SHAP ranked BMI mean the top physiologic predictor, with diastolic BP slope mapping to orthostatic hypotension - affecting ~20% of community-dwelling older adults and linked to falls (OR 1.73) - and RDW mean reflecting inflammation that may precede overt anemia.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: By mean |SHAP| on 5,000 held-out observations, the top physiologic trajectory features were BMI mean (0.141)...
claims.reason: Results section: Feature importance. The paper explicitly states that BMI mean was the top physiologic predictor by SHAP ranking.

claims.text: Diastolic BP slope maps to orthostatic hypotension, which affects ~20% of community-dwelling older adults and is linked to falls (OR 1.73).
claims.poster_quote: SHAP ranked BMI mean the top physiologic predictor, with diastolic BP slope mapping to orthostatic hypotension - affecting ~20% of community-dwelling older adults and linked to falls (OR 1.73) - and RDW mean reflecting inflammation that may precede overt anemia.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Diastolic blood pressure slope, the leading trajectory-specific feature (0.104), connects to a well-characterized autonomic pathway. Orthostatic hypotension affects ∼20% of community-dwelling older adults and is significantly associated with fall risk (meta-analytic OR = 1.73; 95% CI 1.50–1.99).
claims.reason: Discussion section: Mechanistic interpretation. The paper explicitly links diastolic BP slope to orthostatic hypotension and provides the prevalence and odds ratio.

claims.text: RDW mean reflects inflammation that may precede overt anemia.
claims.poster_quote: SHAP ranked BMI mean the top physiologic predictor, with diastolic BP slope mapping to orthostatic hypotension - affecting ~20% of community-dwelling older adults and linked to falls (OR 1.73) - and RDW mean reflecting inflammation that may precede overt anemia.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: RDW mean (0.094) is a notable finding: elevated RDW reflects erythropoietic instability driven by chronic inflammation, iron deficiency, and oxidative stress, and has been independently associated with frailty, all-cause mortality, and functional decline in older adults.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Mechanistic interpretation. The paper explicitly states that RDW mean reflects inflammation and is associated with functional decline.

claims.text: At the trajectory model’s precision, roughly one in three flagged patients is a true positive versus one in four at baseline.
claims.poster_quote: At the trajectory model’s precision, roughly one in three flagged patients is a true positive versus one in four at baseline, since AUROC alone can stay high at low prevalence despite poor positive-class detection.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The trajectory model’s AUPRC of 0.380 - approximately 3.4× the no-skill baseline of 0.111 - suggests that at moderate recall levels, roughly one in three flagged patients would be a true positive, a ratio far more compatible with clinical workflow integration than the baseline model’s one-in-four rate.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Why AUPRC improvement matters more than AUROC improvement. The paper explicitly compares the precision of the trajectory model and baseline.

claims.text: Independence from utilization proxies supports use in safety-net and rural practices.
claims.poster_quote: Independence from utilization proxies supports use in safety-net and rural practices, with alert thresholds of 0.20 or 0.25 matched to local referral capacity and risk refreshed each time a lab result is filed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: This finding has direct implications for health equity: it means the model retains strong performance even when applied to patients with infrequent healthcare contact, a critical requirement for deployment in safety-net settings, federally qualified health centers, and rural practices serving populations with the highest functional decline burden.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Informative observation as confounder and signal. The paper explicitly supports the claim about use in safety-net and rural practices.

claims.text: Alert thresholds of 0.20 or 0.25 can be matched to local referral capacity.
claims.poster_quote: Independence from utilization proxies supports use in safety-net and rural practices, with alert thresholds of 0.20 or 0.25 matched to local referral capacity and risk refreshed each time a lab result is filed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: To operationalize alerts, a probability threshold must reflect local referral capacity. At 0.20 - where NRI over baseline was 0.077 - roughly one in three flagged patients is a true positive (AUPRC 0.380). At 0.25, where NRI gain was highest (0.124), a higher-specificity alert could trigger comprehensive geriatric assessment.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Toward clinical deployment. The paper explicitly discusses matching alert thresholds to local referral capacity.

claims.text: Risk is refreshed each time a lab result is filed.
claims.poster_quote: Independence from utilization proxies supports use in safety-net and rural practices, with alert thresholds of 0.20 or 0.25 matched to local referral capacity and risk refreshed each time a lab result is filed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: It runs as a background process, updating risk scores each time a new laboratory result is filed.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Toward clinical deployment. The paper explicitly states that risk is refreshed with each new lab result.

claims.text: ICD-10 outcomes reflect documented recognition.
claims.poster_quote: Limits: ICD-10 outcomes reflect documented recognition, median imputation ignores clinical context, CRP and vitamin D give little signal from selective ordering, and external validation against gait speed is still needed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: ICD-10-coded outcomes capture documented recognition rather than objective functional performance, introducing potential detection bias.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Limitations. The paper explicitly states that ICD-10 outcomes reflect documented recognition.

claims.text: Median imputation ignores clinical context.
claims.poster_quote: Limits: ICD-10 outcomes reflect documented recognition, median imputation ignores clinical context, CRP and vitamin D give little signal from selective ordering, and external validation against gait speed is still needed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Median imputation assigns a population-level central value regardless of clinical context; future studies should assess sensitivity to the assumed missingness mechanism and consider multiple imputation approaches.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Limitations. The paper explicitly states that median imputation ignores clinical context.

claims.text: CRP and vitamin D give little signal from selective ordering.
claims.poster_quote: Limits: ICD-10 outcomes reflect documented recognition, median imputation ignores clinical context, CRP and vitamin D give little signal from selective ordering, and external validation against gait speed is still needed.

claims.paper_evidence: CRP (82%–98% missing across variants) and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (80%–88%) exhibited the greatest overall sparsity, limiting their trajectory signal.
claims.reason: Results section: Study Population and Missingness. The paper explicitly states that CRP and vitamin D provide little signal due to selective ordering.

claims.text: External validation against gait speed is still needed.
claims.poster_quote: Limits: ICD-10 outcomes reflect documented recognition, median imputation ignores clinical context, CRP and vitamin D give little signal from selective ordering, and external validation against gait speed is still needed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: External validation in independent health systems is required before deployment, particularly given that biomarkers were selected a priori based on known pathophysiologic links - validation against cohorts using objective functional endpoints such as gait speed or SPPB would test generalizability beyond administratively-defined decline.
claims.reason: Discussion section: Limitations. The paper explicitly states that external validation against gait speed is needed.

claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A critical gap therefore exists: no large-scale study has systematically evaluated whether temporal trajectory features derived exclusively from routine laboratory measurements, without diagnosis codes, medications, or functional assessments, can predict pre-clinical functional decline.
claims.reason: Introduction section. The paper explicitly states that no large-scale study has tested whether routine lab trajectories alone predict pre-clinical decline.

claims.text: Cases came from ICD-10 mobility codes in All of Us (OMOP, Controlled Tier v8).
